answer.text: Official answer A; editorial worked explanation: An isotope of X must finish with the same proton number Z but a different mass number A. One alpha emission changes A by −4 and Z by −2. Each beta-minus emission leaves A unchanged and raises Z by 1. One alpha followed by two beta-minus emissions therefore gives net ΔZ=−2+2=0 and ΔA=−4, producing an isotope of X. This is option A.

The graph shows the expected number N of undecayed nuclei against time. What is the half-life of the isotope?

A. 20 minutes
B. 15 minutes

answer.text: A. Initially N=1000. At N=500, the graph gives t≈1200 s. This is 20 minutes.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Actinium-225 has 89 protons and undergoes alpha decay. How many protons and neutrons does the daughter nucleus contain?

A. 89 protons;225 neutrons
B. 89 protons;136 neutrons
C. 87 protons;221 neutrons
D. 87 protons;134 neutrons

answer.text: D. Alpha emission removes 2 protons and 2 neutrons. The daughter has Z=87 and A=221, so its neutron number is 221−87=134.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Which transformation occurs inside a nucleus during beta-plus decay? ν denotes an electron neutrino and ν̄ an electron antineutrino.

A. n → p + e⁻ + ν
B. p → n + e⁺ + ν
C. n → p + e⁻ + ν̄
D. p → n + e⁺ + ν̄

answer.text: B. A proton becomes a neutron, emitting a positron and an electron neutrino: p→n+e⁺+ν.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

answer.text:
Official answer D checked; editorial worked explanation:

In beta-plus decay a proton changes to a neutron, so the mass number stays constant and the atomic number decreases by one. A positron and an electron neutrino are emitted. Only option D shows Mg-23 to Na-23 plus e+ and nu_e. Therefore D.

evidence.detail: Official key page 3 gives D; explanation independently authored and checked.

Subtract background first: the source count rate is 580-20 = 560 s^-1. One hour is four 15-minute half-lives, so the source rate becomes 560/16 = 35 s^-1. Add the unchanged background: 35+20 = 55 s^-1. Therefore B.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Stable ¹³¹₅₄Xe has total binding energy 1.105 GeV. (a)(i) Define binding energy. (a)(ii) Calculate the nuclear mass in GeV c⁻² using proton mass 0.938 GeV c⁻² and neutron mass 0.940 GeV c⁻². (b)(i) Define isotopes using ¹³³₅₄Xe and ¹³¹₅₄Xe. (b)(ii) Radioactive ¹³³₅₄Xe is less stable; compare its binding energy per nucleon with that of ¹³¹₅₄Xe.

answer.text: Official markscheme results; editorial worked explanation: (a)(i) Binding energy is the minimum energy required to separate a nucleus completely into its individual nucleons; equivalently it is released when those nucleons assemble. (a)(ii) ¹³¹Xe contains 54 protons and 77 neutrons. The separated-nucleon mass is 54(0.938)+77(0.940)=123.032 GeV c⁻². The bound nucleus has less mass by E_b/c²=1.105 GeV c⁻², so M=123.032−1.105=121.927≈122 GeV c⁻². (b)(i) Isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers. (b)(ii) For the comparison requested between these two nearby xenon isotopes, the source identifies ¹³¹Xe as stable and ¹³³Xe as radioactive; the intended inference is that ¹³¹Xe has the greater binding energy per nucleon.
answer.evidence: Official November 2024 Physics SL Paper 2 markscheme 8824-9594M checked on PDF page(s) 9–10; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the visible source task.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The source graph shows activity against time for a pure sample of ¹³³₅₄Xe. Estimate its half-life.

answer.text: Official markscheme accepted range 5.2–5.4 days; editorial worked explanation: The initial activity is about 9.0×10⁷ Bq. Half of this is 4.5×10⁷ Bq. Reading the time at which the curve reaches 4.5×10⁷ Bq gives approximately 5.3 days, within the official 5.2–5.4 day range.
answer.evidence: Official November 2024 Physics SL Paper 2 markscheme 8824-9594M checked on PDF page(s) 10; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the visible source task.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: By reference to binding energy, explain why the combined mass of the separate nucleons of a nucleus is greater than the mass of the bound nucleus.

answer.text:
Official markscheme checked; editorial worked explanation:

When separate nucleons bind to form a nucleus, energy equal to the binding energy is released. By E = Δmc², this released energy corresponds to a decrease in rest mass. Conversely, that energy must be supplied to separate the nucleus completely, so the separated nucleons have greater combined mass than the nucleus.

evidence.detail: May 2024 SL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6711M, PDF page 12, checked against this exact subpart.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Binding energies per nucleon are Th-228: 7.645074 MeV, Ra-224: 7.679917 MeV, and He-4: 7.073915 MeV. Determine the energy released in Th-228 → Ra-224 + He-4.

answer.text:
Official markscheme checked; editorial worked explanation:

Energy released equals total final binding energy minus initial binding energy: Q = 224(7.679917) + 4(7.073915) − 228(7.645074) MeV = 5.520 MeV. This is positive because the products are more tightly bound in total; in joules it is about 8.84 × 10⁻¹³ J.

evidence.detail: May 2024 SL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6711M, PDF page 12, checked against this exact subpart.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: By reference to binding energy, explain why the combined mass of the separated nucleons is greater than the mass of the nucleus they form.

answer.text: Official markscheme reasoning; editorial worked explanation: When separated nucleons bind to form a nucleus, energy equal to the binding energy is released. By mass-energy equivalence E=Δmc², releasing energy reduces the system's rest mass. Equivalently, energy must be supplied to separate the nucleus completely, so the separated nucleons have the greater total mass by Δm=E_b/c².
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics HL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6708M checked on PDF page(s) 13; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the source task.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The binding energies per nucleon are Th-228: 7.645074 MeV, Ra-224: 7.679917 MeV, and He-4: 7.073915 MeV. Determine the energy released in ²²⁸₉₀Th→²²⁴₈₈Ra+⁴₂He.

answer.text: Official markscheme result 5.520 MeV; editorial worked explanation: Total binding energy of the products is 224(7.679917)+4(7.073915) MeV, while that of the parent is 228(7.645074) MeV. Thus Q=224(7.679917)+4(7.073915)−228(7.645074)=5.520 MeV, positive because the products are more tightly bound overall. This is 8.84×10⁻¹³ J.
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics HL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6708M checked on PDF page(s) 13; editorial explanation independently recalculated against the source task.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Tritium activity decreases from A₀ to A₀/8 in 37.0 years. (a) State what is meant by the half-life of a radioactive nuclide. (b) Calculate the half-life of tritium.

answer.text: Official markscheme results: half-life is the time for the activity, or the number of undecayed parent nuclei, to fall to half its initial value; tritium’s half-life is 12.3 years. Editorial worked explanation: A₀/8=A₀(1/2)³, so 37.0 years represents three half-lives. Therefore T₁/₂=37.0/3=12.3 years.
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics SL Paper 2 TZ1 markscheme 2224-6705M checked on PDF page(s) 11; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: In the fusion reaction ²₁H+³₁H→⁴₂He+¹₀n, energy is released. Outline why mass is not conserved in this reaction.

answer.text: Official markscheme point: some reactant mass is converted to energy. Editorial worked explanation: The products have less rest mass than the reactants. The mass decrease Δm corresponds to the released energy through ΔE=Δmc². Total mass–energy is conserved even though rest mass alone is not.
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics SL Paper 2 TZ1 markscheme 2224-6705M checked on PDF page(s) 12; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Tritium activity decreases from A₀ to A₀/8 in 37.0 years. (a) State radioactive half-life. (b) Calculate tritium’s half-life.

answer.text: Official markscheme results: half-life is the time for activity or undecayed parent nuclei to halve; T₁/₂=12.3 years. Editorial worked explanation: A₀/8=A₀(1/2)³, so three half-lives take 37.0 years and one takes 37.0/3=12.3 years.
answer.evidence: Official May 2024 Physics HL Paper 2 TZ1 markscheme 2224-6702M checked on PDF page(s) 11; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: An experiment on ionized hydrogen identifies nuclei with the same proton number, Z=1, but different masses. Explain what this shows about hydrogen isotopes.

answer.text: Hydrogen has isotopes: nuclei with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. The extra neutrons change the nuclear mass while the element remains hydrogen.

parts.display_text: Rubidium-87, with proton number 37, decays into strontium-87, with proton number 38. Identify the type of radioactive decay.

answer.text: Beta-minus decay. A neutron becomes a proton while an electron and an electron antineutrino are emitted; A stays 87 and Z increases by 1.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The neutral atomic mass of rubidium-87 is 86.91 u and its proton number is 37. Calculate its binding energy per nucleon. Use hydrogen atomic mass 1.007825 u, neutron mass 1.008665 u and 1 u c²=931.5 MeV. Electron binding energies may be neglected.

answer.text: There are 37 protons and 50 neutrons. Using hydrogen atomic masses cancels the 37 electron masses on each side: Δm=37×1.007825+50×1.008665−86.91=0.812775 u. Total binding energy≈757.10 MeV, so binding energy per nucleon≈757.10/87=8.70 MeV.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A sample initially contains only xenon-142 nuclei. After 6.0 s, the number of nuclei that have decayed is 31 times the number of xenon-142 nuclei remaining. Calculate the half-life, showing your reasoning.

answer.text: For every remaining nucleus, 31 have decayed, so the remaining fraction is 1/32 = (1/2)⁵. Five half-lives have passed in 6.0 s. The half-life is 6.0/5 = 1.2 s.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Uranium-238 (proton number 92) undergoes a sequence containing only alpha and beta-minus decays, ending at lead-206 (proton number 82). How many alpha and beta-minus particles are emitted?

A. 8 alpha and 6 beta-minus
B. 8 alpha and 10 beta-minus
C. 16 alpha and 6 beta-minus
D. 16 alpha and 22 beta-minus

answer.text: A. Each alpha decay reduces nucleon number by 4, so (238 − 206)/4 = 8 alpha particles. This leaves proton number 92 − 16 = 76; six beta-minus decays raise it to 82.
